title: Browser-only rules could become unconditional DNS allows or replace the last-good allow generation
reproduction: Local StringReader inputs on offline, isolated API34 arm64 emulator-5566; real in-memory Room and SQLite inserts. Import ordinary/wildcard/suffix/dnsmasq controls mixed with cosmetic and option-scoped browser records. Separately import nested conditional branches and an unsupported-only candidate after setting a known-good active generation. Reviewed finding: tasks/audit-2026-11-25/deep-signoff/input-safety.md.
expected: No browser-only input contributes an allow row. Preserve supported rules and kinds; skip conditional branches without interpreting them. A rejected revision must leave zero candidate rows and keep the prior active rule resolvable.
observed: Same final test APK on pre-fix app: actual cosmetic and conditional host counts each 1 instead of 0; unsupported-only candidate incorrectly succeeded; global cosmetic-only input was accepted as empty. All four focused tests failed as expected.
fix: Allow path strips only unambiguous inline comments, preserving the dnsmasq hash target; wildcard fallback validates the entire rule. Ordered allow-source reader skips both arms of browser conditionals before parser fan-out, counts rejected records and rejects unbalanced sections. Existing failure cleanup retains the preceding generation; ordinary comment-only policy and block-mode parser unchanged.
